ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there are two slides of equal length. The height \(AC\) of the left slide is equal to the horizontal length \(DF\) of the right slide. What is the sum of the degrees of the incline angles \(\angle ABC\) and \(\angle DFE\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\angle ABC + \angle DFE = 90^\circ$, the reasoning is as follows:\\
From the problem, we know that both $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$ are right-angled triangles, with $BC = EF$ and $AC = DF$.\\
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
BC = EF\\
AC = DF
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ (by HL criterion),\\
$\therefore \angle ABC = \angle DEF$,\\
$\because \angle DEF + \angle DFE = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC + \angle DFE = \boxed{90^\circ}$.

On the right side, the horizontal base DF, the vertical side DE, and the hypotenuse EF form a right triangle DFE, where DE is perpendicular to DF, and EF is the slide on the right. The problem states that the two slides have equal length, so BC = EF; it also states that the left height AC is equal to the right horizontal length DF, so AC = DF.

Then reason: Triangles ABC and DEF are both right triangles, and their hypotenuses BC and EF are equal, and one right side AC and DF are equal, so by the hypotenuse-leg (HL) criterion, △ABC ≅ △DEF. Corresponding angles are equal, so ∠ABC = ∠DEF. In right triangle DEF, ∠DEF and ∠DFE are two acute angles, and they are complementary, so ∠DEF + ∠DFE = 90°. Substituting ∠ABC = ∠DEF gives ∠ABC + ∠DFE = 90°.
